subject: Geopolitics
title: The Semiconductor Supply Chain
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Semiconductor Supply Chain.

hook.text: A single chip factory costs $20 billion and takes five years to build. Only three companies can make leading chips.

buildup.text: TSMC in Taiwan, Samsung in Korea, and Intel in the US dominate. The rest of the world is a customer.

discovery.text: Chips go into everything: cars, weapons, medical devices, phones. Whoever controls chips controls modern life.

twist.text: The US banned advanced chip equipment sales to China. The Netherlands and Japan enforced it. A tech blockade formed.

climax.text: China is spending $100 billion to build domestic capacity. But catching up in chip tech may take a generation.

punchline.text: The tiniest product drives the biggest power struggle.

quiz.question: Why is the semiconductor supply chain a geopolitical issue?
options: Semiconductors are used exclusively in weapons
Only a few companies can make advanced chips, creating dependence
Chips are made from rare materials found only in China
